relationships.description: The collaboration counts the component as one of its participating members, while the component stays independently deployable and may also belong to other collaborations.
relationships.evidence: A docker-compose file, Helm umbrella chart, or architecture document lists the component as a member service of the named collaboration, for example among the declared participants of a saga.

relationships.description: The collaboration is the joint actor whose members together carry out the interaction, so the interaction's outcome is the value the collaboration exists to produce.
relationships.evidence: A saga or choreography definition, such as a Temporal workflow, Step Functions state machine, or event-flow document, has every step executed by member components of the collaboration.

relationships.description: The collaboration's combined behaviour is what makes the externally visible service available, so the service's operations exist only because the members work together.
relationships.evidence: An API gateway route or service-catalog entry for the service is fulfilled by orchestrating calls across several member components of the collaboration.

relationships.description: The collaboration cannot perform its collective behaviour unless the component, such as a shared platform service outside its membership, is available.
relationships.evidence: The member components' runtime configuration or readiness checks reference the component's endpoint, and the collaborative flow fails when that component is unavailable.

relationships.description: The collaboration relies on a separate interaction, such as a prerequisite handshake or upstream saga, completing before its own collective behaviour can proceed.
relationships.evidence: The collaboration's workflow or choreography definition waits on the completion event or callback emitted by that other interaction.

relationships.description: The collaboration's members must reach the interface, such as an external API endpoint or message channel, to carry out their joint behaviour.
relationships.evidence: Client configuration in the member components, such as a base URL, generated gRPC stub, or queue subscription, targets that interface.

relationships.description: The collaboration's members must share and agree on the data object, such as a common event payload or saga state record, to coordinate their joint work.
relationships.evidence: A shared contract package, such as a protobuf message or Avro schema, is imported by multiple member components and exchanged between them during the collaborative flow.

relationships.description: The collaboration offers a single access point, such as a gateway endpoint or shared topic, through which consumers reach the services its members deliver jointly.
relationships.evidence: An API gateway, ingress, or BFF controller configuration mounts a route that fans out to the member components and is documented as the collaboration's entry point.

notes: delivers-value is a traceability predicate. ArchiMate would use assigned-to for collaboration→interaction and realizes for collaboration→service. depends-on component overlaps aggregates when the target is a member. depends-on interaction partly inverts the performer relationship. provides interface conflicts with the interface definition, which says an interface is owned by a component.
